name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
description: OpenThoughts3-1.2M is a 1.2 million example open-source dataset for training reasoning models via supervised fine-tuning (SFT). It contains question-response pairs across math (850,000), code (250,000), and science (100,000) domains. The dataset is constructed through a systematic pipeline involving question sourcing from diverse sources, question filtering using LLM-based methods, deduplication, sampling multiple answers per question (16x), and using QwQ-32B as the teacher model to generate reasoning traces. The dataset was developed through 1,000+ controlled experiments to identify the best data generation strategies.
license: Multiple licenses apply to source datasets; see Appendix Q for details. Key sources include Apache 2.0 (Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, QwQ-32B), CC BY 4.0 (OpenMath-2, OpenCodeReasoning), CC BY-SA 4.0 (StackExchange CodeGolf, StackExchange Physics), and OpenAI Terms of Use.
creator: OpenThoughts Team (Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, and many others from Stanford University, University of Washington, BespokeLabs.ai, Toyota Research Institute, UC Berkeley, UT Austin, UCLA, LAION, NYU, UNC Chapel Hill, ASU, and other institutions)
citeAs: Guha, E., Marten, R., Keh, S., Raoof, N., Smymis, G., et al. Data Recipes for Reasoning Models. 2025. https://www.open-thoughts.ai/blog/ot3
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed through a multi-stage automated pipeline: (1) Question sourcing from 27 code sources, 21 math sources, and 14 science sources including fully synthetic (LLM-generated), semi-synthetic (LLM using existing data as seeds), and non-synthetic (human-written) questions. (2) Question mixing selecting top 1-2 sources per domain. (3) Question filtering using LLM-based difficulty or response length methods. (4) Deduplication using exact or fuzzy match. (5) Sampling 16 answers per question from QwQ-32B as teacher model. The pipeline was informed by 1,000+ controlled ablation experiments.
rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No explicit discussion of missing data in the dataset. Some question sources produced fewer datapoints than needed, in which case questions were repeated until the desired amount was reached.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions sourced from: (Code) StackExchange CodeGolf, OpenCodeReasoning, KodCode-V1, CodeFeedback, dolphin-coder, and 22 other sources; (Math) OpenMath-2-Math, NuminaMath-1.5, MathPile, AutoMathText, DeepMath-103K, and 16 other sources; (Science) StackExchange Physics, Organic Chemistry PDFs (SCP-116K and textbooks), CQADupStack-Physics, Camel-AI Physics/Chemistry/Biology, and other sources. Answers/reasoning traces generated by QwQ-32B teacher model.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were deduplicated using exact match deduplication for math and science, and no deduplication for code. For math and science, 16 answers were sampled per question from QwQ-32B. For code, 16 answers were also sampled per question with no deduplication. Deduplication used Normalized Indel similarity score via Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) metric. The dataset was decontaminated against evaluation benchmarks using Indel similarity (75% threshold) and N-gram similarity (N=13) methods.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Pipeline steps: (1) Question sourcing from diverse sources; (2) Question mixing - selecting top 1-2 sources per domain; (3) Question filtering - difficulty-based filtering with GPT-4o-mini for code, response length filtering with GPT-4.1-mini for math and science; (4) Deduplication - exact deduplication for math and science, no deduplication for code; (5) Sampling 16 answers per question from QwQ-32B; (6) No answer filtering applied. Decontamination against evaluation benchmarks was performed using Indel similarity and N-gram similarity. GPT-4o-mini was used for question generation requiring an LLM for some sources.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Reasoning traces (thinking tokens) and answers were generated by QwQ-32B as the teacher model for all domains. The teacher model generates long chain-of-thought responses enclosed in <think> and </think> tokens followed by the final answer. For earlier dataset versions (OpenThoughts-114K), DeepSeek-R1 was used as the teacher with LLM-based verification. For OpenThoughts3, no answer filtering/verification was applied as it did not improve performance. GPT-4o-mini was used for question difficulty labeling and response length filtering during question selection.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: QwQ-32B (primary teacher model for OpenThoughts3); GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1-mini/nano used for question filtering and labeling; DeepSeek API used for pipeline experiments at ~$300 per 31,600-sample dataset.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Extensive ablation experiments (1,000+) were conducted to evaluate annotation strategies. Key findings: (1) QwQ-32B outperforms DeepSeek-R1 and Phi-4-Reasoning-Plus as teacher despite scoring lower on benchmarks; (2) No answer filtering strategy outperformed using all answers without filtering; (3) Sampling 16 answers per question provides effective data scaling; (4) Removing self-reflection from reasoning traces caused 49.1% relative performance drop, indicating long reasoning structures are essential.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 16 answers (reasoning traces) generated per question from the teacher model QwQ-32B.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: QwQ-32B (teacher model for answer/reasoning trace generation), GPT-4o-mini (question difficulty filtering, response length filtering, question generation for some sources, verification experiments), GPT-4.1-mini (response length filtering for math and science), GPT-4.1-nano (response length filtering), gemini/gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05 (OCR for organic chemistry PDFs), FastText classifiers (question and answer filtering), OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (embedding-based filtering), Evalchemy (evaluation framework).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset released on Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-thoughts/OpenThoughts3-1.2M. Codebase released at https://github.com/open-thoughts/open-thoughts. The OpenThoughts project has gone through multiple generations (BespokeStratos-17K, OpenThoughts-114K, OpenThoughts2-1M, OpenThoughts3-1.2M), suggesting ongoing development. All assets and code stored in the open-thoughts Hugging Face organization.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables open-source development of reasoning models competitive with proprietary systems. Safety analysis shows that SFT on reasoning data inadvertently degrades safety alignment: OpenThinker3-7B trained on this data has a harmfulness rate of 55.5% on HarmBench (up from 14.5% for the base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), indicating a trade-off between reasoning capability and safety. The authors note future work should incorporate safety-specific datasets to mitigate these risks.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset focuses exclusively on math, code, and science domains, limiting coverage to these reasoning-intensive areas. Question sources include both human-written (competition problems, forums) and synthetic (LLM-generated) questions, with no clear pattern emerging between synthetic and non-synthetic quality. The dataset does not include reinforcement learning data. Distilled reasoning models trained on this data show generalization deficits, exhibiting strong performance fluctuations on reasoning-invariant problem perturbations (Alice in Wonderland evaluation).
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to math, code, and science domains and does not cover reinforcement learning training data. The paper did not explore staged SFT or curriculum learning. Cross-domain transfer effects when domains are mixed are not fully understood. The dataset does not include safety-specific data, leading to degraded safety alignment in trained models. Some benchmarks saturate at large scales (AMC23, MATH500) and others do not respond to scale (HLE). The interaction between question diversity and answer diversity across different domains, dataset sizes, and model scales remains an open question.
rai:dataUseCases: Primary use case: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) of language models to develop reasoning capabilities in math, code, and science. The dataset was used to train OpenThinker3-7B (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct base) achieving state-of-the-art results among open-data 7B models. Also applicable to training reasoning models on other base models (demonstrated with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct). Not recommended for: reinforcement learning training without modification, safety-critical applications without additional safety alignment, or domains outside math, code, and science.
